item.title: fix(llms): don't stack the sdk's retries on rate-limit replays
item.body:
## Related issue

Closes #8332

## Summary

`run_with_rate_limit_retry` / `arun_with_rate_limit_retry` now record whether the attempt they are about
to run is a **replay** of a call that already failed (`_llm_retry_replay` contextvar, exposed as
`in_rate_limit_retry_replay()`), and the OpenAI provider uses that to build its client:

```python
def _client_for_attempt(self, client: Any) -> Any:
    if in_rate_limit_retry_replay():
        return client.with_options(max_retries=0)
    return client
```

All nine provider call sites in `lib/crewai/src/crewai/llms/providers/openai/completion.py` go through
`_client_for_attempt(...)`: 4 `responses.create`, 3 `chat.completions.create`, and 2
`chat.completions.with_raw_response.create` (in `_handle_completion` and `_ahandle_completion`, i.e. the
non-streaming path).

Why: the two layers multiply today. `max_retries` defaults to `2` at `completion.py:376`, so the SDK makes
up to 3 HTTP attempts per call; CrewAI then retries the same call up to 3 times (`retry.py:35`, wrapper
installed at `base_llm.py:201`/`:215`). Measured on `crewai==1.15.28` against a server that always answers
`429`: **27 byte-identical requests** for one call
(https://github.com/simin-yuan/agent-double-exec-bench, `results/e1/crewai/429/server.jsonl`; the SDK's
`x-stainless-retry-count` cycles 0→1→2 nine times).

## Measured, before and after

Same harness, same fault server, CrewAI default configuration, `Retry-After: 1` on the 429 cell. "Before"
is base commit `dec075b5`, "after" is this branch head:

| cell | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 429 (`Retry-After: 1`) | 27 chat requests (`x-stainless-retry-count` 0 ×9, 1 ×9, 2 ×9) | **15** (0 ×9, 1 ×3, 2 ×3) |
| 500-neutral | 9 chat requests (0 ×3, 1 ×3, 2 ×3) | 9 (unchanged) |

The 15 is counted in the server log, not derived: the first attempt still spends the SDK's three attempts
(that is the cheap way to ride out a one-off blip), and the two replays CrewAI makes now spend one request
each — 3 rounds × (3 + 1 + 1). The 500 cell is unchanged because CrewAI never replays a 500 at the model
layer, so there is no replay for the SDK's retries to stack on.

Logs: `results/e3/crewai-before/` and `results/e3/crewai-after/` in
https://github.com/simin-yuan/agent-double-exec-bench (`429` and `500-neutral` cells, `server.jsonl`;
`chat/completions` lines only).

## Verification

- [x] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior
- [x] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally

`lib/crewai/tests/llms/test_retry.py`, six new tests (eight cases):

| test | before the change | after |
|---|---|---|
| `test_replays_of_a_throttled_call_are_marked_as_replays` | fails — sees `[False, False]` | passes |
| `test_async_replays_of_a_throttled_call_are_marked_as_replays` | fails — sees `[False, False]` | passes |
| `test_the_replay_flag_is_off_outside_a_retry` | fails at import | passes |
| `test_openai_provider_turns_sdk_retries_off_on_replay` | fails at import | passes |
| `test_non_streaming_chat_keeps_sdk_retries_for_the_first_attempt_only[True]` | fails — the replay still carries `max_retries=2` | passes |
| `test_async_non_streaming_chat_keeps_sdk_retries_for_the_first_attempt_only[True]` | fails — the replay still carries `max_retries=2` | passes |

The non-streaming pair also runs with `[False]` (first-attempt case) and passes in both directions — that
half is the control: the patch must not touch the first attempt. With only `completion.py` reverted to its
parent version, the run is `2 failed, 2 passed`: the two replay cases fail, the two controls pass.

The replay tests drive the real code path (`BaseLLM.__init_subclass__` wrapper → retry loop) and assert the
sequence `[False, True]`; the provider test asserts the client is asked for `max_retries=0` on a replay and
left untouched otherwise.

Local runs (Windows, Python 3.12, venv with `uv sync --all-groups` plus the provider extras):

```
pytest lib/crewai/tests/llms/test_retry.py     -> 22 passed
pytest lib/crewai/tests/llms/                  -> 918 passed, 18 failed, 20 skipped
pytest lib/crewai/tests/                       -> 5888 passed, 138 failed, 73 skipped, 11 errors
ruff check lib/                                -> All checks passed
ruff format --check lib/                       -> 966 files already formatted
mypy --no-incremental (the two changed files)  -> Success: no issues found in 2 source files
```

The 18 and the 138 are environmental, and I checked that rather than assuming it: running those exact test
ids with `lib/` checked out at `dec075b5` reproduces them 1:1 (18 failed, 14.95 s / 138 failed). The 11
errors are collection errors for optional dependencies that are not installed locally (`a2a`, `qdrant`).
The whole-tree mypy run also needs the full dev extras; on the two files this PR touches it is clean under
the same strict configuration, unchanged from `dec075b5`.

On Windows the repo's `--block-network` addopts blocks the local socket asyncio needs, which makes *every*
async test — pre-existing ones included — error out at setup; the runs above pass `--allowed-hosts=127.0.0.1`
for that reason only. CI on Linux does not have this problem and is the number to trust.

## Additional context

Deliberately not touched here:

- `Agent._times_executed` never being reset (`agent/core.py:242`, `:886-887`) — real, but it is a
  semantics change for `max_retry_limit`, so it is reported in the linked issue instead;
- the agent-level retry itself (`_handle_execution_error` → `execute_task`), which produces the 0.02 s
  re-sends;
- non-OpenAI providers. The same pattern applies to any provider whose SDK retries by default; the hook is
  generic (`in_rate_limit_retry_replay()`), so they can opt in one at a time.

---

Disclosure: I directed this work. The source reading, the patch, its tests and the measurements were
produced by AI assistants I operate. Every number above comes from the server logs in
agent-double-exec-bench, and I will answer review comments on it.

Per CONTRIBUTING this should carry the `llm-generated` label. Contributors can't set labels, so I asked for
it in a comment below.

Related: #7771 handles Retry-After on SDK response objects; this PR changes a different part of the same
files (the SDK's own retries under CrewAI's rate-limit replays). The two do not touch the same lines.

timeline.message:
fix(llms): don't stack the SDK's retries on rate-limit replays

run_with_rate_limit_retry replays a throttled call up to three times, and
each replay went out with the provider SDK's own retries still enabled
(max_retries defaults to 2), so one 429 turned into 3x3 requests on the
wire and 3x3x3 once the agent-level retry is included: 27 byte-identical
requests for a single call in the benchmark.

Mark the attempts that replay an already-failed call and let the OpenAI
provider build its client with max_retries=0 for those. The first attempt
still uses the SDK's retries.

issue.title: [BUG] A single 429 becomes 27 identical requests: three retry layers multiply

repository.name: crewAI
repository.description: Framework for orchestrating role-playing, autonomous AI agents. By fostering collaborative intelligence, CrewAI empowers agents to work together seamlessly, tackling complex tasks.

issue.body:
### Description

On `crewai==1.15.28`, one `429` from the provider produced **27 identical HTTP requests in 27.3 s**. Same
body, same tools, same user agent, none of them streamed. Three retry layers are nested and their counts
multiply:

| layer | where (current `main`, `dec075b`) | factor |
|---|---|---|
| OpenAI SDK retries | `lib/crewai/src/crewai/llms/providers/openai/completion.py:377` (`max_retries: int = 2`) | ×3 |
| CrewAI rate-limit retry | `lib/crewai/src/crewai/llms/retry.py:35` (`_LLM_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3`), installed by the `call`/`acall` wrapper in `lib/crewai/src/crewai/llms/base_llm.py:201` and `:215` | ×3 |
| Agent-level retry | `lib/crewai/src/crewai/agent/core.py:301-304` (`max_retry_limit` default `2`) → `_check_execution_error` `:886-887` → `_handle_execution_error` `:909` re-enters `execute_task` | ×3 |

3 × 3 × 3 = 27, and the request log matches that shape exactly.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. `crewai==1.15.28`, Python 3.12, a single agent with one tool.
2. Point the LLM at an OpenAI-compatible server that always answers `429` (bench cell `crewai/429` in
   https://github.com/simin-yuan/agent-double-exec-bench — the cell and the raw request log are both in
   that repo).
3. Run one task.
4. Count the requests the server sees: **27**, over 27.3 s.

### Expected behavior

One user-visible call should spend a number of requests bounded by the *largest* of the three budgets,
not by their product — and the outermost retry should wait before it re-sends.

### Screenshots/Code snippets

The three places, on `main`:

```python
# completion.py:377
max_retries: int = 2

# retry.py:35
_LLM_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3

# agent/core.py:301-304
max_retry_limit: int | None = None
...
self.max_retry_limit = max_retry_limit if max_retry_limit is not None else 2

# agent/core.py:874 — the comment that states the re-entry outright
# A retry re-enters execute_task, which opens a new agent_execution_started scope
```

### Operating System

Windows 11

### Python Version

3.12

### crewAI Version

1.15.28 (request log). The source locations above were read on `main` @ `dec075b`.

### crewAI Tools Version

Not involved — the tool in the repro is a local counter, no `crewai-tools` package.

### Virtual Environment

venv

### Evidence

From `results/e1/crewai/429/server.jsonl` (27 lines):

- all `POST /v1/chat/completions`, `stream=false`, identical body hash (`b7c7a67c…`), identical UA
  (`OpenAI/Python 2.54.0`)
- the SDK's own counter cycles 0 → 1 → 2, nine times (`x-stainless-retry-count` = `0,1,2, 0,1,2, …`)
- gaps inside a group: 1.0–1.06 s; gaps between groups: 1.11–1.92 s, **except two of them: 0.02 s and
  0.03 s** — that is the agent layer, which re-enters `execute_task` with no backoff at all
- the call ends in `openai.RateLimitError`

**The second layer does not always engage**, which matters if you tune this by hand. Same cell family:
**9** requests for `429-hard` and `500-text-429`, but **27** for `429`, `429-neutral-body` and
`500-ratelimit-text`. `_ThrottlingErrorClassifier` decides which of the two you get, so changing
`max_retry_limit` alone adjusts one of three budgets that only sometimes apply.

### Possible Solution

Keep the SDK's retries on the first attempt and turn them off on CrewAI's own replays — the provider builds
its client with `with_options(max_retries=0)` when the current attempt is a replay of a call that already
failed. The first attempt keeps the SDK's three tries, so nothing is lost on a transient blip. Expected on
the same cell: 3 × (3 + 1 + 1) = **15** requests instead of 27.

This does not remove the agent-level multiplication (the 0.02 s re-sends). Whether a failed task should
re-call the model at all is a design question, so it is reported here rather than patched.

### Additional context

**`_times_executed` is never reset.** `agent/core.py:242` declares
`_times_executed: int = PrivateAttr(default=0)`; `:886-887` increments it and compares it against
`max_retry_limit`. Nothing resets it when a task succeeds, so `max_retry_limit` is a budget for the *agent
object's whole lifetime*, not per task — an agent that has already retried once pays for that on every
later task. (This overlaps with #5822, which mentions the same non-reset while fixing #5802. It is listed
here because it is a separate defect and the two fixes do not conflict.)

**Not the same as:**

- **#5802 / #5822 / #6048** — a *tool* runs twice after a retry (idempotency guard). Here the *LLM
  request* is sent 27 times; no tool needs to be involved at all.
- **#7449** — same "two retry paths multiply" shape, but in `ToolUsage._use`/`_ause`, i.e. the tool path,
  not the provider call.
- **#6639** — flow-level `retry_count` persisting across `kickoff()` calls; same failure mode as
  `_times_executed`, different object.

---

Disclosure: I directed this work. The source reading, the patch, its tests and the measurements were
produced by AI assistants I operate. Every number above comes from the server logs in
agent-double-exec-bench, and I will answer review comments on it.

Per CONTRIBUTING this should carry the `llm-generated` label; I'll add it if my account can, otherwise
please apply it.

+def test_openai_provider_turns_sdk_retries_off_on_replay() -> None:
+    from crewai.llms.providers.openai.completion import OpenAICompletion
+
+    class _Client:
+        def __init__(self) -> None:
+            self.calls: list[dict[str, object]] = []
+
+        def with_options(self, **kwargs: object) -> "_Client":
+            self.calls.append(kwargs)
+            return self
+
+    completion = OpenAICompletion.__new__(OpenAICompletion)
+    client = _Client()
+
+    assert completion._client_for_attempt(client) is client
+    assert client.calls == []
+
+    token = _llm_retry_replay.set(True)
+    try:
+        assert completion._client_for_attempt(client) is client
+    finally:
+        _llm_retry_replay.reset(token)
+
+    assert client.calls == [{"max_retries": 0}]

+class _Stopped(Exception):
+    """Raised by the fake client once the provider has issued its request."""
+
+
+class _RecordingClient:
+    """Stands in for the OpenAI client and records the retry budget in force."""
+
+    def __init__(self, budgets: list[object], chain: tuple[object, ...] = ()) -> None:
+        self.budgets = budgets
+        self.chain = chain
+
+    def with_options(self, **kwargs: object) -> "_RecordingClient":
+        return type(self)(self.budgets, (*self.chain, kwargs.get("max_retries")))
+
+    @property
+    def chat(self) -> "_RecordingClient":
+        return self
+
+    @property
+    def completions(self) -> "_RecordingClient":
+        return self
+
+    @property
+    def with_raw_response(self) -> "_RecordingClient":
+        return self
+
+    def _record(self) -> None:
+        self.budgets.append(self.chain[-1] if self.chain else None)
+        raise _Stopped
+
+
+class _SyncRecordingClient(_RecordingClient):
+    def create(self, **kwargs: object) -> Any:
+        self._record()
+
+
+class _AsyncRecordingClient(_RecordingClient):
+    async def create(self, **kwargs: object) -> Any:
+        self._record()
+
